context.title: For My Name's Sake
context.summary: When elders come to inquire, God retells Israel's history as one long rebellion in Egypt, the wilderness and the land, yet promises a new exodus that will purify the people.
context.background: This message is dated about 591 BC (v. 1). Again and again God held back judgment 'for my name's sake' (vv. 9, 14, 22), to protect his reputation among the nations. Verse 25, 'statutes that were not good,' is difficult; many read it as God handing a stubborn people over to their own chosen practices. In the KJV, verses 45–49 begin the next oracle; Hebrew Bibles place them in chapter 21.

customs.note: A shepherd counted sheep one by one as they passed under his staff, separating some out (Leviticus 27:32).

watchFor: The repeated cycle: rebellion, threatened wrath, mercy 'for my name's sake.'

people.name: Israel
people.summary: One who follows on another’s heels; supplanter, (Gen. 25:26; 27:36; Hos. 12:2-4), the second born of the twin sons of Isaac by Rebekah. He was born probably at Lahai-roi, when his father was fifty-nine and Abraham one hundred and fifty-nine years old.

places.name: Egypt
places.summary: The land of the Nile and the pyramids, the oldest kingdom of which we have any record, holds a place of great significance in Scripture.

places.name: Bamah
places.summary: A height, a name used simply to denote a high place where the Jews worshipped idols (Ezek. 20:29).

places.name: Negeb
places.summary: Heb. Negeb, that arid district to the south of Palestine through which lay the caravan route from Central Palestine to Egypt (Gen. 12:9; 13:1, 3; 46:1-6).

events.title: Prophecies of Ezekiel
events.summary: Passage: Ezekiel 1:1–48:35. People: Ezekiel. Lasted about 23 years.
